title: Elixir
text: “Those guys… Motoyasu-kun and the others are different from a Spirit-Chosen Child in every conceivable way. Theirs are arrogant souls that could never be chosen.”
It really was a foolish, run-of-the-mill ambition, and Ark seemed to think it was a waste of breath even asking, pulling a necklace from his pocket and giving it a light shake.
“Spirits. Please, lend me your strength.”
A dazzling light burst forth—and my spear vanished, flying straight into Ark’s hand. The jewel at its center was blazing with a brilliance I had never seen before—it was practically blinding, I say!
“Ah… did Motoyasu-kun’s Sacred Weapon come here? Sorry about that. I’ll borrow it for a bit.”

With a crackling sound, the Sacred Weapon shifted shape, the spear refining itself into a shield that drifted to hover alongside the necklace. Ark took up both shield and spear at once, readying them in tandem—spear and shield, the equipment of a knight, indeed! My spear could do something like that!? Certainly, as a piece of protective equipment, it made sense that a shield was within its scope of possibility—after all, a Sacred Weapon is a bundle of potential. It likely carried some protective power, much like Father’s shield. But… I did not have the right to wield that power, I say.

“Ha, what’s with the attitude? This cat here doesn’t seem to get a joke when he hears one—real troublesome. A guy who gets mad over something this small, calling himself a god-slayer? Don’t make me laugh.”
“If the other party gets angry, you call it a joke? That sounds like a pretty pathetic excuse from a pretty pathetic criminal.”
There was no excuse in the world for hurting a Filolial-sama as some kind of joke. Every last one of these people was rotten to the core.
“I’ll keep watching no matter what you do, but try not to cause any trouble for Motoyasu-kun and the others, alright?”

With a click, Ark turned the shield forward. Right then, Hou-kun appeared beside me and the Filolial, who was trembling with eyes shut tight, pretending not to hear anything—standing guard as if to protect us. A faint warmth, like a barrier, spread out around us, gentler than the one before.
“Take your punishment for making us this angry! Eat this!”
“Buhiiiii!”
“Buh!”
“Bu-bu-buu!”
The pigs allied with the reincarnators charged at Ark. Naturally, the reincarnators themselves were mixed in among them too.

“You arrogant lot, trying to become gods—that throne isn’t suited for the likes of you. To the accomplices of the ringleaders gathered here: if you don’t want to die, repent from the bottom of your hearts, right here, right now. Do that, and I’ll let it go. You have ten seconds!”

A voice—or something more like telepathy, impossible to fully describe—that seemed capable of reaching anywhere echoed through the surroundings. It seemed Ark was giving the reincorporators’ allies a grace period. My spear, held in Ark’s grip, began wrapping itself in ominous red-black flames and shifting form. It was obvious at a glance that it had become a cursed weapon. And during those ten seconds, Ark was attacked again and again, yet dodged or deflected every single blow, I say.
“That was your final chance, and it’s passed. Let it be carved into your flesh! I’ll chant it in time with you all.”
“I knew this was coming, but there’s no helping it, huh. Really, cats are cruel…”
With a sharp motion, Ark readied spear and shield and began chanting the skill.

“The name of the punishment I have decreed for these sinners who falsely proclaim themselves foolish gods is the Path That Brings Death. Perish, screaming in agony, devoured by the jaws of a dragon that feasts on immortal flesh and blood!”
“Elixir Blutopfer!”
Splurt! Blood gushed forth from every inch of Ark’s body, and the surrounding area began turning into a sea of blood!?
“Self-destruction!? No, wait, everyone! Don’t drink that blood!”
“This is our chance—I heard his blood can even be used as a weapon coating, so if we smear it on our gear and—”

Just as one reincarnator was giving that advice to the surrounding pigs… countless bear-traps shaped like dragon jaws rose up out of the sea of blood, appearing beneath the feet of everyone in the settlement who had not repented—everyone except the reincarnators themselves—and bit down, devouring them again and again.
“Buhyaaaaaaaa!?”
“Gu, guh—ah!? It, it hurts! I—I’m gonna die— someone, h-help—”
“Buhiiii—!?”
The reincarnators were struck speechless, forced to watch as the pigs allied with them were devoured before their eyes.
“Gyaaaa—”
“Buhyaaaaaaa—”
The death screams of the massacre echoed loudly enough to be heard even from outside the building.
“Wha—”
“Y-you bastard!”
“You son of a—!”

The Curse Skill, having risen from the sea of blood, sank back down, swallowing its victims whole. My spear drifted gently out of Ark’s hand and returned to me. But I couldn’t tear my eyes away from Ark’s blood-soaked figure. That sight… was so painful to see that it reminded me of Father when he fought the Pope. And yet I myself didn’t have so much as a scratch on me…
“Liberation Fireheal X!”

I knew full well that a Curse Skill’s curse would drastically weaken any healing magic—yet even so, I couldn’t help wanting to heal Ark’s wounds, I say. But for some reason… I couldn’t target the healing magic at all. Even when I tried to cast it, all I felt was as though I were aiming at empty space, nothing there. It was as if there had never been anything there to begin with.
“How dare you—my comrades!”
“You… you devil!”
“Calling yourself a god-slayer and pulling off a massacre like this—there’s no way that’s allowed!”
“Something like this can’t be forgiven! I’ll kill you!”

The reincarnators, enraged at seeing everyone in the settlement they had gathered slaughtered before their eyes, poured power into their weapons—but the moment the scattered blood touched their weapons, those weapons flared with a blinding light and flew from their hands.
“The numbers game is about to end. Watching your faces twist in agony was quite the pleasure.”
Oh, Ark’s expression in that moment struck me as strangely divine, I say. The Demon Lord and Father had their suspicions, but that display of skill and power really could be described no other way.
“Guh… my strength—it’s draining out of me!?”
“How much more are you going to take from us before you’re satisfied!? You bastard!”
“How much more? Only as much as you took. A life for a life. Your own sins are what handed down this punishment—nothing more.”
Ark declared this flatly, like an executioner.
“I’m definitely going to kill you! No one’s ever pissed me off this much!”
“Tch… like hell I’d accept a result like this! I’ll just rewind time with my magic, that’s all!”

I recognized that look in the reincarnators’ eyes. Takt had worn that same expression when his pigs were executed right in front of him. One of the reincarnators tried to cast some kind of spell, but it burst into flame and fizzled out—was that intentional?
“Rewinding time? You really think we’d let you do that, in a situation like this?”
It seemed Hou-kun had interfered.
“Don’t you dare get in my way! Get outta here!”
“So you’re saying you can’t rewind time unless you kill this one first?”
“I’ll kill him!”
“There won’t be a next time for any of you.”

Countless souls hovered above Ark’s outstretched hand. As for where those souls had come from—they were the ones who’d died to the Curse Skill just now. They were visible to the naked eye, no need for a Soul Eater Spear to see them.
“Ahh, and here I wanted to burn that rotten lot to a crisp in the flames of purgatory. Guess it can’t be helped, since I have to give way this time.”
Hou-kun muttered this, watching the thrashing souls gathered in Ark’s hand.
“Sorry, but I’m going to use a different method on these guys.”
“Yeah, yeah. I know.”
Having finished talking with Hou-kun, Ark turned to look my way and smiled. That shift in temperature… left me with such a strange feeling, I say.
“Motoyasu-kun, you’re a kind one, aren’t you. Trying to cast healing magic on me, in a situation like that.”
The wounds and curses eating away at Ark’s whole body vanished smoothly, as though nothing had ever happened. Whether he had healed himself or not, I couldn’t say.
“…It’s almost over now.”

Answering thus, Ark raised a hand toward the gathered souls. The color of the glowing wings unfurled on his back began to shift—like a smear of every paint color mixed together—before eventually transforming into a transparent black, the color of the void itself. At the same time, the souls Ark held his hand over condensed into that same transparent black, forming something like orbs of magic that burst and mingled together. It was obvious at a glance just how horrifying this attack was.
Before long, the burst orbs had split into countless fragments. With a firm push of his hand, Ark sent them scattering, flying toward the reincarnators.
